name: Pineapple upside-down cake
origin: Popularised in the United States in the 1920s after canned pineapple rings became widely available; a butter-and-brown-sugar caramel and pineapple rings are laid in the pan first, the batter poured over, and the whole cake inverted after baking.

process.name: prepare pan topping
process.description: melt butter and brown sugar in the pan, then arrange pineapple rings in the caramel

process.name: cream butter and sugar for the batter
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: add eggs and fold in flour
process.description: beat in eggs, then fold in flour, leavening and salt

process.name: bake and invert
process.description: pour the batter over the pan topping and bake, then invert onto a plate while still warm

notes: The batter itself is a standard equal-weights butter cake (see victoria-sponge.json, pound-cake.json). The butter-brown-sugar caramel and pineapple rings are a separately-prepared component assembled in the pan before the batter is poured in — real and described in the process steps, but kept out of the ingredient list per catalog.ts's scope note, since baker's percentage describes the one mixed batter, not a second component that shares its pan and bake but is never actually mixed into it.
